title: Intermediate Portuguese for Business, Health, and Legal Purposes
description: Prepares students to reach intermediate high proficiency in Portuguese, focusing on language use in the business, health, and legal fields.
notes: Heritage speakers of Portuguese are encouraged to take the course; may consult with instructor or Portuguese Program Director for placement. Not open after PORT 204.

description: Women authors of the Portuguese-speaking world and their relationship to the cultural, historical, literary, and sociopolitical questions raised by their texts.
notes: Taught in English.

title: Portuguese and Brazilian Cinema and Culture
description: Main movements and productions of Portuguese and Brazilian cinema. Social factors and representations of national identities.
notes: Taught in English.

notes: Taught in English.

description: Developing advanced proficiencies in grammar, reading, and writing, based on models from modern Luso-Brazilian literary and non-literary texts.
notes: Taught in Portuguese. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Portuguese course taught in Portuguese.

title: Contemporary Luso-Brazilian Civilization
description: Cultural, ethnic, geographic, historical, political, and social factors of modern Brazil and Portugal.
notes: Taught in Portuguese. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Portuguese course taught in Portuguese.

title: Methods in Teaching Spanish and Portuguese as a Second Language
description: Teaching of Spanish and Portuguese as a second language: contemporary theory and methods. Emphasizes training in teaching techniques to develop students’ presentational, interpersonal, and interpretative skills.
notes: Taught in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Proficiency in Portuguese not required for students specializing in Spanish; proficiency in Spanish not required for students specializing in Portuguese. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish and Portuguese courses.
